title: Why isn't the average 45 km/h?
hook: A slow outward leg and a fast return cover equal distances.

knows: the quantities named in the question
doesNotKnow: The outward trip takes 2 h and the return takes 1 h. Divide the full 120 km by the full 3 h: 40 km/h. You spend longer at the slower speed.

misconception: The alternative answers in the prediction appear plausible without the stated physical model.
objective: The outward trip takes 2 h and the return takes 1 h. Divide the full 120 km by the full 3 h: 40 km/h. You spend longer at the slower speed.

claims.text: The outward trip takes 2 h and the return takes 1 h. Divide the full 120 km by the full 3 h: 40 km/h. You spend longer at the slower speed. Each leg has constant speed; stops and acceleration are excluded.
claims.source: Average speed = total distance / total time; 120/(60/30+60/60)=40 km/h.

recall.question: You travel 20 km at 20 km/h and 20 km at 40 km/h. What is your average speed?
recall.why: 40 km divided by 1.5 h is about 26.7 km/h.
